text_blocks.snippet: Type 2 diabetes often develops slowly over years, and many people do not notice symptoms in the early stages.

list.snippet: Frequent urination: Excess sugar builds up in the blood, and your kidneys try to flush it out by producing more urine (especially at night).
Increased thirst and dry mouth: Because you are losing more fluids through frequent urination, you feel constantly dehydrated and thirsty.
Fatigue and weakness: Your cells cannot absorb glucose properly for energy, leaving you unusually tired.
Blurred vision: High blood sugar can cause fluid to shift and swell the lenses of your eyes, making it hard to focus.
Slow-healing cuts and sores: High blood sugar damages blood vessels and impairs circulation, slowing down your body's ability to repair wounds.
Tingling or numbness: High glucose levels can damage peripheral nerves (neuropathy), often causing a pins-and-needles feeling or numbness in the hands or feet.
Darkened skin patches: A condition called acanthosis nigricans causes velvety, dark patches of skin in body folds like the neck, armpits, or groin, which signals strong insulin resistance.
Frequent infections: Higher blood sugar weakens the immune system, leading to recurring urinary tract infections (UTIs) or yeast infections.
Unexplained weight changes: Your body may start burning fat and muscle for fuel if it cannot use glucose properly, leading to weight loss, though some people experience weight gain.
